newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says ends critical dialogue with Iran.
newsitem.headline: Germany says ends critical dialogue with Iran.

text.p: Germany said on Thursday that it was ending its policy of "critical dialogue" with Iran for the foreseeable future after a German court accused Iran's leaders of ordering the killings of dissidents in Berlin.
"The government is certain that it will not be taking part in this critical dialogue for the foreseeable future," the German Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

The policy of critical dialogue, championed by Germany, was initiated by the European Union back in 1992 in an effort to gain influence in Iran. Major allies, above all Britain and the United States, accuse Iran of state terrorism.
Iran has denied all responsibility for the murders and on Thursday the speaker of the Iranian parliament Ali Akbar nateq-Nouri dismissed the court verdict as "political".
The Foreign Ministry statement also said EU nations were considering joining Germany in recalling their ambassadors from Tehran in response to the Berlin court verdict.
"The government regrets this development, especially since the Iranian and German peoples have enjoyed friendly relations for well over 100 years," the statement ended.
